question: In order to enable trainees to exercise their rights without fear of reprisals and terminate a working arrangement that puts their health, safety or dignity at risk, Parliament is calling for the introduction of a specific right of withdrawal.

This right would empower any trainees in imminent, grave danger, or facing harassment, violence or any other serious violation of their rights, to cease their activity temporarily or quit without incurring adverse consequences, such as loss of remuneration or non-validation of their training. In view of the above: 1.
Does the Council support the introduction of a right of withdrawal for trainees without reprisals?
If not, on what grounds is it opposed to such a move?
How will it make sure that trainees can report any threats or abuse and protect themselves effectively in such situations without fear of reprisals or unfair dismissal from their traineeship?
